findings.title: Add E2E coverage for the missing-package guidance. This install hint is user-facing, so keep it covered by a CLI regression in the E2E suite.
findings.label: trivial
findings.note: This is a request for more test coverage of a hint message and points to no defect.

findings.title: `warnOnVersionSkew` loses the prod/dev split, so its alignment command misclassifies `stash`. `skewed.map(({ pkg }) => pinnedSpec(pkg))` is passed as the *prod*
findings.label: incorrect
findings.note: There is no warnOnVersionSkew at head; align commands are built through splitProdDev, which puts stash in dev.

findings.title: Print alignment commands when missing packages and skew coexist non-interactively. This path installs only missing packages, but never displays `alignCommands`.
findings.label: valid
findings.note: When missing packages and skew both occur non-interactively, the code takes the install path and never prints alignCommands, which contradicts the docstring's promise to print the exact align commands.

findings.title: Verify all first-party packages in the manual-install guidance. Checking only `@cipherstash/stack` does not detect skew in the integration adapter (affects skil
findings.label: trivial
findings.note: Only a documentation wording suggestion for the skill notes; init itself already checks adapter skew.

findings.title: Do not report success while alignment failed or skew remains. An alignment command can fail while every package remains present at its old version.
findings.label: valid
findings.note: The post-install re-check only tests presence, so a failed align command leaves the old versions present and still logs 'Stack dependencies installed.' even though skew remains.
